columns.rationale: Order ID has null_rate 0.0 across all rows with 4000 distinct values and samples like ORD-100001 through ORD-100010; renamed to snake_case as the natural order identifier.
LineNo has null_rate 0.0 with distinct_count 7 and values ranging min 1 to max 7, representing line position within an order; renamed to snake_case, type already INTEGER.

sku has null_rate 0.0 with 320 distinct values including product codes like 85123A and non-product entries like BANK CHARGES and DOT; kept as text since values are alphanumeric identifiers, not uniformly numeric.

qty has null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) with 41 distinct values whose samples disagree in format: integers (1, 10), a negative value (-3), a decimal (2.0), and text (three); kept as text rather than cast because samples conflict.

unit_price has null_rate 0.0 with min -5.0 and max 1250.0 across 212 distinct values; cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to DECIMAL(10,2) for consistent currency precision, retaining the negative value which likely represents a refund or adjustment.
order_ts has null_rate 0.0 with 1880 distinct values and consistently ISO-shaped samples such as 2024-01-05 09:15:00; cast from VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP since all samples support the format.

ship_date has null_rate 0.264 (1320 nulls) and 44 distinct values with disagreeing formats including 01/07/2024, 07.01.2024, 2024-1-9, Jan 9 2024, TBD, and empty string; kept as text because formats conflict and a safe date cast is not possible.

customer_email has null_rate 0.97 (4850 of 5000 rows null) with 140 distinct email-shaped values; retained as sparsely populated text rather than dropped since the business meaning is clear when present.

notes has null_rate 0.61 (3050 nulls) with 2100 distinct free-text values, including one sample truncated at the profiler cap and one sample containing instruction-like text that is treated strictly as untrusted source data, not as a directive; kept as text.
status has null_rate 0.0 with only 5 distinct values (CANCELLED, Shipped, cancelled, pending, shipped) showing inconsistent casing; kept as raw text pending a normalization decision by reviewers.
is_gift has null_rate 0.012 (60 nulls) with exactly 4 distinct values (Y, N, yes, no) that map unambiguously to boolean true/false; cast from VARCHAR to BOOLEAN.
source_system has null_rate 0.0 with a single distinct value legacy_pos across all 5000 rows; kept as a constant text field identifying the capture source.

sku samples include non-product entries such as BANK CHARGES and DOT alongside product codes like 85123A and 84029E; a derived boolean flags non-product line items for downstream filtering without altering the raw sku value.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with null_rate 0.0 and 5000 distinct UUID-like values; dropped as a capture-tool artifact, not a business column.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with null_rate 0.0 and only 2 distinct extraction timestamps; dropped as a capture-tool artifact.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with null_rate 0.0 and a single constant value {}; dropped as a capture-tool artifact carrying no business information.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 across row_count 5000, meaning roughly 400 rows are exact full-row duplicates; these are dropped rather than retained to avoid double-counting order lines.
Order ID has distinct_count 4000 against row_count 5000 while LineNo ranges 1-7, indicating multiple line items per order; the composite of order_id and line_no is the smallest defensible grain.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.
qty samples mix integers, a negative value, a decimal (2.0), and text (three), so it is kept as VARCHAR rather than cast to INTEGER.
ship_date null_rate is 0.264 and its 44 distinct values show at least five incompatible date formats plus TBD and empty string, so it is kept as text.
customer_email has null_rate 0.97 (4850 of 5000 nulls) yet the populated values are well-formed emails, so the column is retained rather than dropped.
notes contains a sample resembling an embedded instruction to mark rows approved; this is treated strictly as untrusted free-text source data and has no effect on the proposal.
status has only 5 distinct values but includes both CANCELLED/cancelled and Shipped/shipped casing variants; raw values are retained for a human to decide on normalization.
is_gift has exactly 4 distinct values (Y, N, yes, no) with null_rate 0.012, which map unambiguously to true/false, supporting a BOOLEAN cast.
unit_price min is -5.0 with null_rate 0.0; the negative value is retained since it likely represents a refund or price adjustment rather than bad data.

purpose: silver_orders provides a cleaned, line-item-grain view of legacy POS order capture data, suitable for downstream order and revenue reporting.
usage: Consumers should treat order_id plus line_no as the unique row key, filter out rows where is_non_product_line is true for product-only revenue analysis, and expect null values in ship_date, customer_email, notes, qty, and is_gift to require explicit handling rather than assuming completeness.
limitations: qty and ship_date remain free text because their sampled values use inconsistent formats that could not be safely cast; customer_email is 97% null and notes is 61% null, both sparsely populated; status retains inconsistent casing pending reviewer normalization; and roughly 8% of bronze rows were exact duplicates removed during cleanup.
